title: Rank error of MultiQueues under unrestricted insertion orders
formal: Determine the worst-case per-deletion expected rank error R(q,T) of the sequential MultiQueue process, up to universal constant factors, for all q≥2 and T≥2.
definitions: Start q empty exact priority queues. Each insertion places its distinct real key into an independently uniform queue. Each deletion independently samples two queue indices uniformly with replacement and removes the smaller of their minima, treating an empty minimum as +∞. If both sampled queues are empty, repeat sampling until a nonempty queue is selected; no other operation interleaves with these retries. A tie from sampling the same queue removes its minimum once. All inserted keys are globally distinct. A valid finite operation sequence has at most T operations, contains at least one deletion and never deletes when the total structure is empty. Its operations and key ordering are fixed before all randomness; insertions smaller than past deletions are allowed. For a specified deletion t, its error E_t is the number of currently stored keys strictly smaller than the returned key, immediately before deletion. Define R(q,T)=sup_{σ,t} E[E_t], with the supremum over these oblivious sequences and their deletion positions. The expectation includes every random insertion and deletion choice, including empty retries. Only relative ordering of keys matters.
answer_criterion: Supply an explicit nonnegative function g(q,T) and universal constants 0<c≤C<∞ with a complete Lean-checked proof c g(q,T)≤1+R(q,T)≤C g(q,T) for every integer q≥2,T≥2. The formula for g must be evaluable in time polynomial in q+T and cannot call a MultiQueue simulator, enumerate operation histories or refer back to R. A sequence-averaged or monotone-insertion-only bound is insufficient.
context: The source explicitly identifies general quality analysis as open; its discussed bounds restrict how new keys compare with previously removed keys.

import_provenance.original_title: Rank error of MultiQueues under unrestricted insertion orders
import_provenance.original_statement: For the basic MultiQueue with q internal priority queues, uniformly random insertions, and deletion of the smaller minimum from two random queues, determine the worst-case expected rank error over oblivious operation and key sequences. In particular, does an O(q) bound survive when insertions can introduce keys smaller than previously deleted keys?
